title: The selected 2012 HD 85512 HARPS exposure has excess line width and a velocity difference before nightly correction
abstract: We test an extreme HD 85512 HARPS exposure selected by earlier campaign work. Relative to 17 nearby control exposures, its paired velocity difference is -45.94 m/s. Of this change, -34.29 m/s is present before nightly correction. Applied corrections add -11.66 m/s. The DRS line width is 52.98 m/s above its local median, and the SERVAL width index is also high. H-alpha and signal to noise are near local values. Three ESO raw headers give the same target, mode and input velocity. The Sun is 28.27 degrees below the horizon. These checks do not support a correction-only or bright-twilight explanation. They do not identify the cause. Shared spectra, selected controls, no direct profile fit and no independent instrument limit the result. No new planet is found. Original code, aggregate evidence, exact input hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Source data remain external.

display.caption: The selected event has a velocity difference before nightly correction and excess line width across four local control windows. Robust scales are descriptive, not detection significance.

citations.reason: Selects the extreme night. We add correction accounting, line-profile tests and raw-header checks.
